title: C# Quiz
description: Review the ideas from the lessons. Take your time. After each answer, read the note that explains the rule. You can try again.

questions.question: What is C#?
questions.explanation: C# is a programming language. .NET supplies tools and services that help C# programs run.
options: A language for writing computer programs

questions.question: Inside a console project folder, type dotnet ___ to build and run it.
questions.explanation: dotnet run builds the current project and starts the program. Run it from the project folder.

questions.question: What number appears?
questions.explanation: score starts at 3. The += 2 statement adds 2 and stores 5.

questions.question: What is printed after changing b?
questions.explanation: int is a value type. b gets its own copy, so changing b does not change a.

questions.question: Which symbol lets int___ score = null; hold a number or no value?
questions.explanation: int? is a nullable int. It can hold an integer or null, which means no value.

questions.question: What is missing after the case action?
questions.explanation: A C# switch case cannot simply fall into the next case after an action. Add break to leave it.
options: A break, return, throw, or other valid exit

questions.question: Fill the gap: int Twice(int n) ___ n * 2;
questions.explanation: The arrow is a short way to write a method with one expression. Here the result is n times two.

questions.question: What does Show(name: "Asha", age: 10) use?
questions.explanation: Each value is paired with an input name. That makes it clear which value goes to which input.

questions.question: Why can this child not override Speak?
questions.explanation: An override needs a parent method marked virtual, abstract, or already override. Mark Animal.Speak virtual.
questions.code:
class Animal { public void Speak() {} }
class Dog : Animal { public override void Speak() {} }
options: The parent method is not virtual
Dog is too short a name

questions.question: What is printed for these two records?
questions.explanation: Records compare their stored values by default. Both Colour values are Blue, so they are equal.
questions.code:
Console.WriteLine(new Badge("Blue") == new Badge("Blue"));
record Badge(string Colour);

questions.question: In what order are these letters shown?
questions.explanation: try writes A and reports an error. catch handles it and writes B. finally runs next and writes C.

questions.question: Fill the gap inside an async method: string text = ___ File.ReadAllTextAsync("notes.txt");
questions.explanation: await waits for this operation to finish without blocking the waiting thread. Then it gives you the result.

questions.question: What is a test marked [Theory] useful for in xUnit?
questions.explanation: A theory test accepts inputs. InlineData can give it several examples to check.
options: Checking the same rule with several input sets
